cards.text: A cloud fills the house of the LORD, and the priests can't stand there to minister, because the glory of the LORD fills the house of God (2 Chronicles 5:13-14). Then Solomon, king of Israel and David's son, speaks: “The LORD has said that He would dwell in the thick cloud.”

cards.question: True or false: Solomon tells the LORD he has built Him a house to dwell in forever.

cards.text: Then the king turns around to face the whole assembly of Israel standing there. And he blesses them all.

cards.question: Solomon blesses the LORD for doing with His own hand what He spoke with His mouth. Who did God make that promise to?

cards.text: Solomon repeats what the LORD said back then. Since the day He brought His people out of Egypt, He hadn't chosen a city from any tribe to build a house for His Name, or anyone to rule over His people.

cards.question: But now, the LORD says, He has chosen ___ for His Name to be there, and David to be over His people Israel.

cards.text: Here's the backstory, friend. Building a house for the Name of the LORD was in David's heart first.

cards.question: Building a house for the LORD's Name was in David's heart. What does the LORD tell David about having that in his heart?

answers.text: He did well to have it in his heart
He should have asked a prophet first
He was reaching too high for a king

cards.question: True or false: The LORD tells David that he is the one who will build the house.

cards.text: It's David's own son who will build it, and now Solomon sits on his father's throne with the house built, just as the LORD promised. The LORD said it, the LORD did it, and meanwhile I've been promising my ovens a deep clean since the day I got here.

cards.question: Solomon says he has placed something inside the house he built. What is it?

answers.text: The ark holding the LORD's covenant
The sword that belonged to Goliath

cards.text: Then Solomon stands before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly, up on a bronze platform he had made, five cubits long, five wide and three high. I've stood on a gold base as long as I can remember, friend, and it has NEVER gotten me three cubits off the ground.

cards.question: Solomon steps up onto that bronze platform in front of the whole assembly. What does he do up there?

answers.text: Kneels and spreads his hands toward heaven
Reads the law of Moses out loud
Holds up the tablets for all to see

cards.question: True or false: Solomon begins his prayer by telling the LORD there are other gods just like Him in heaven.

cards.text: Solomon says God kept His promise to David this very day. Now he asks God to keep another one: David will never fail to have a man to sit on the throne of Israel.

cards.question: That throne promise comes with an if. David's descendants must guard their way to walk in God's ___, as David did.

cards.text: Solomon asks God to confirm what He promised David. Then he stops and asks the big one: will God really dwell with people on earth?

cards.question: Solomon wonders if God will really dwell with people on earth. What does he say can't contain God?

cards.text: This temple Solomon built can't hold God either, he says, and friend, I can't even admit when one of my cookies comes out LOPSIDED. Still, he asks the LORD to regard the prayer and plea of His servant.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon asks for God's eyes to be open toward the temple day and night.

cards.text: And it's not just Solomon's prayers. He asks God to hear His people Israel too, whenever they pray toward this place.

cards.question: When Israel prays toward the temple, where does Solomon ask God to hear them from?

answers.text: From the top of Mount Zion

cards.question: Solomon asks God to hear from heaven, His dwelling place, and then to ___.

cards.text: Now Solomon gets specific, one case at a time. First: when a man sins against his neighbor and has to take an oath, he comes before the altar in this temple.

cards.question: When a man who sinned against his neighbor takes an oath at the altar, Solomon asks God to judge: condemning the ___ man and justifying the ___ man.

cards.text: Next: Israel is defeated by an enemy because they've sinned against God. Then they turn back and confess His name.

cards.question: When defeated Israel turns back and confesses God's name, where does Solomon picture them praying and pleading?
True or false: When defeated Israel turns back and prays, Solomon asks God to forgive them and give them a brand new land of their own.

cards.text: Next: the skies are shut and there's no rain, because the people have sinned. If they pray toward this place and turn from their sins, Solomon asks God to forgive them and send rain on the land.

cards.question: When the skies are shut because Israel has sinned, and they turn from their sins, Solomon asks God to forgive them and teach them. What does he ask God to teach them?

answers.text: The good way they should walk
How to store water for dry years

cards.text: Then Solomon names more hard times: famine, plague, blight, mildew, locusts, grasshoppers, enemies besieging their cities, and whatever sickness may come. He leaves nothing off the list.

cards.question: In those hard times, each person prays with his hands spread out toward this temple. Solomon asks God to forgive and repay each man by his ways, since only God knows the ___ of men.

cards.text: All of this so Israel will fear God and walk in His ways all the days they live in the land. Next: a foreigner, not one of God's people Israel, comes from a distant land because of God's great name, and he prays toward this temple.

cards.question: Solomon asks God to answer the foreigner who prays toward the temple. What does Solomon say will happen then?

answers.text: All peoples will know His name and fear Him
The foreigner will bring the temple rich gifts
Israel's enemies will all be put to shame

cards.question: True or false: When Israel goes to war and prays toward the city and the temple, Solomon asks God to uphold their cause.

cards.text: Next: the people sin against God, and Solomon says it straight: there is no one who does not sin. That includes a certain stamper, friend, so this mustache is NOT pointing at anybody.

cards.question: Solomon pictures God angry with His people who sinned, handing them over to an enemy who takes them as ___ to a land far or near.

cards.text: Then, in the land of their captors, they come to their senses. They confess they've sinned and done wrong, and they return to God with all their heart and soul.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon pictures Israel, held captive in an enemy land and turning back to God, praying in the direction of their land, the city God chose and the temple.

cards.text: Solomon asks God to hear them from heaven, uphold their cause and forgive His people. Then once more, he asks for God's eyes to be open and His ears attentive to the prayer offered in this place.

cards.question: Solomon calls on the LORD God to arise. What does he ask the LORD to enter, together with the ark of His might?

cards.text: Solomon asks for God's priests to be clothed with salvation, and for His godly ones to rejoice in goodness.

Last of all, Solomon asks God not to reject His anointed one, and to remember His loving devotion to His servant David. That's where the prayer ends, friend, but hold on to your apron, because this story is NOT done yet.
